newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka buys end-March diesel, jet from Glencore.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka buys end-March diesel, jet from Glencore.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought by tender 220,000 barrels of gas oil and 40,000 barrels of jet fuel from Swiss trader Glencore for March 27-28 delivery, a CPC source said on Friday.

The 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil was purchased at 65 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, and jet fuel at 75 cents above Singapore spot quotes, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Colombo.
The tender, which attracted five offers, closed on March 5.
In its last tender, CPC bought 220,000 barrels of gas oil and 50,000 barrels of jet fuel from Shell at 95 cents per barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes and 80-cent premium, respectively, c-and-f.
The combined cargo is for March 9-10 deliveries.

With the latest tender, Sri Lanka has bought a total of 660,000 barrels of gas oil and about 140,000 barrels of jet fuel for March deliveries as a result of the maintenance shutdown at its 50,000-barrel refinery.
The Sapugaskanda refinery closed from maintenance from January 15 and was running at 40,000-bpd as of March 3.
Sri Lanka's tender for early April delivery will be decided next week, the CPC source said.
